originality.rationale: Craig (2022) proves effective all-residue D inequalities only for 2<=t<=10 and conjectures all t. Guy (1958), as reviewed by Sellers–Sills–Mullen (2004), gives the classical binary restricted-partition identity, which proves only generic non-power-of-two adjacency directly. The new exact certificates settle infinitely many missing binary-boundary cases and produce the uniform k>=5 theorem. published-finding corpus queries and accessible own ledger claim comparisons identified no equivalent. Unindexed implicit consequences remain risk.
residual_risks: A previously published but unindexed elementary derivation of adjacent strict-part frequencies may exist.
A more general partition-inequality theorem not located could subsume the k>=5 statement.

value.rationale: Resolves every power-of-two boundary for part-frequency comparisons at k>=5, a key obstruction missed by the standard Guy binary cancellation. Yields an all-moduli theorem for 5<=r<s<=t without asymptotic restrictions, a substantial uniform strengthening along an infinite parameter regime of Craig’s 2022 conjectured inequalities. Reduces the unrestricted adjacent-frequency conjecture to the four small sizes k<=4; the five-factor positivity certificates are structural rather than arbitrary finite samples.
